decisions.reason: As a low-carrying-cost extension of the firm's core second-channel authentication offer, it still preserves option value under uncertainty and fits the move toward secure cross-channel communication.
This appears to be a core architecture layer closely tied to the firm's R&D-heavy identity-security stack, so it is strategically central and inexpensive to keep as an option.

Because it is a more niche hardware-based signature product with higher support and carrying costs in a firm that already has many adjacent software options, resources are more likely to be reallocated away from it.

Even if somewhat specialized, it builds on the firm's compliance and cryptography capabilities and can be retained as a relatively low-cost software option while regulated security demand remains favorable.
